definition: the strangers I have been and will be, and what I feel toward the ones behind me

settled:
Both directions read the same: about half a billion selves each way, sharing one body, meeting at a window seconds wide.

Forward that count is the wall against acting. Backward it carries a feeling.

Grief for the ones who suffered and are gone, gratitude to the ones who kept going so this one is here. I owe my being here to a crowd of strangers who spent themselves getting the body this far, and not one of them is around to be thanked.

The past normally reaches me as facts on file, the feeling stripped out. That time it did not.

What lit it was contrast rather than recall. A session had just gone through the darkest points of my life, and having the distance laid out that starkly made it vivid all at once. I cannot re-feel what they went through. I can see where they stood against where this one does.

They sit on separate scales, both endless. Equal is the least wrong reading, and they never net.

title: The Crowd That Has Been Me
